title: THE NILE AND THE COMING DELIVERER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Pharaoh gave this order to all his people: "Every Hebrew boy that is born you must throw into the Nile, but let every girl live."" - Exodus 1:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends in darkness. Pharaoh drops all pretence and issues a public order: drown the baby boys in the Nile. It is one of the most terrible verses in the Old Testament, and we should not soften it. Evil is real, and children have always been its most defenceless victims.

But hold this alongside what comes next. Out of that very river God would draw Moses, and through Moses He would deliver His people. The place meant to be a grave became the cradle of a rescuer.

Centuries later, another ruler would order the killing of infant boys, and again a child would escape — this time to Egypt — and grow up to be the true Deliverer (Mt 2:16-18). Satan has always attacked the coming of salvation, and he has never once succeeded.

If you are in a dark chapter, remember where this chapter sits. It is chapter one. The story is not finished. The God who was silently preparing Moses in that season is preparing something in yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What darkness am I facing that tempts me to think God has lost control?
2. How does the coming of Christ change the way I read a chapter like this?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, this world's evil is real and I feel it. Thank You that Jesus has already overcome it, and that Your rescue is on the way. Amen.
